title: COPD: The Ophthalmologist's Guide to Systemic Care & Ocular Impact
summary: A comprehensive review of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) through the lens of a board-certified ophthalmologist. This poster bridges systemic pathophysiology with critical perioperative considerations and ocular manifestations for the eye care specialist.

data.title: COPD: The Ophthalmologist's Guide to Systemic Care & Ocular Impact
data.summary: A comprehensive review of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) through the lens of a board-certified ophthalmologist. This poster bridges systemic pathophysiology with critical perioperative considerations and ocular manifestations for the eye care specialist.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: COPD is a common, preventable, and treatable disease characterized by persistent respiratory symptoms and airflow limitation. It is caused by significant exposure to noxious particles or gases. The chronic airflow limitation is caused by a mixture of small airways disease (obstructive bronchiolitis) and parenchymal destruction (emphysema), the relative contributions of which vary between individuals.

rows: Destruction of alveolar walls; capillary loss

sections.title: Diagnosis: The Gold Standard
content: Post-Bronchodilator FEV1/FVC < 0.70 is mandatory for diagnosis.
FEV1: Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second.
FVC: Forced Vital Capacity.
Spirometry is required to differentiate from asthma (irreversible vs. reversible).
Screening: Perform in any patient with dyspnea, chronic cough, or sputum production.

sections.title: Ocular Manifestations & Concerns
content: Hypoxic Retinopathy: Chronic CO2 retention and low O2 can cause retinal venous tortuosity and dilation.
Dry Eye Disease (DED): Increased prevalence due to smoking and oxygen mask airflow ('wind' over the ocular surface).
Steroid-Induced Glaucoma: Chronic systemic or inhaled steroid use increases IOP risk (Ocular Hypertension).
Posterior Subcapsular Cataract (PSC): Higher incidence in patients on long-term corticosteroids for exacerbations.
Normal Tension Glaucoma (NTG): Potential link due to chronic vascular dysregulation and nocturnal hypoxia.
Floppy Eyelid Syndrome: Strongly associated with OSA, which frequently co-exists with COPD (Overlap Syndrome).

sections.title: Perioperative Ophthalmic Considerations
content: Step 1: Assess Positioning - Can the patient lie flat (orthopnea)? Consider 'Incline' surgery for cataracts.
Step 2: Cough Control - Intense coughing during intraocular surgery (e.g., Phaco) risks expulsive choroidal hemorrhage.
Step 3: Anesthesia Choice - Avoid retrobulbar blocks if the patient cannot hold their breath or is highly anxious.
Step 4: Oxygenation - Ensure nasal cannula flow doesn't create 'wind' across the cornea during surgery (DED/Infection risk).
Step 5: Drug Interactions - Topical Beta-blockers (Timolol) are CONTRAINDICATED or must be used with extreme caution (risk of bronchospasm).

sections.title: CRITICAL: Ophthalmic Red Flags
content: Use of Topical Timolol/Beta-blockers in COPD (Potential for fatal bronchospasm).
Sudden vision loss during a coughing fit (Valsalva Retinopathy).
Acute Angle Closure triggered by nebulized anticholinergics (Ipratropium) leaking into the eyes via poorly fitted masks.
Chronic high-dose steroids resulting in IOP > 30 mmHg.

content.explanation: A: Albuterol (SABA); B: Bromides (LAMA/Anticholinergics); C: Corticosteroids (Inhaled); D: Diet/Delivery (Oxygen); E: Exercise/Education (Rehab).

sections.title: Surgical Management & Advanced Care
content: Lung Volume Reduction Surgery (LVRS) for upper-lobe emphysema.
Endobronchial Valves (EBV): One-way valves to collapse hyperinflated segments.
Lung Transplantation: For GOLD 4 patients with high BODE scores.
Pulmonary Rehabilitation: Proven to improve QoL and exercise tolerance.

sections.title: Landmark Clinical Pearls
content: BODE Index: Predictive of mortality (BMI, Obstruction, Dyspnea, Exercise capacity).
Alpha-1 Antitrypsin (AAT) Screening: Every patient with COPD should be tested at least once.
Oxygen Therapy: The only intervention (besides smoking cessation) shown to improve survival in COPD with severe resting hypoxemia.
The 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT): A simple, reproducible marker of functional capacity and prognosis.
ECLIPSE Study: Confirmed that frequent exacerbators (≥2/year) remain frequent exacerbators, regardless of GOLD grade.
